questions.q: James Clerk Maxwell published his theory of electromagnetism in 1864. What was his central achievement?
options: He measured the speed of light using a rotating mirror
He unified electricity and magnetism into one theory, expressed in four equations, and showed they are features of a single electromagnetism
He discovered that magnetic poles can be separated into isolated monopoles
He proved experimentally that radio waves carry energy across empty space
questions.explanation: Maxwell, a Scottish physicist, linked all the electric and magnetic effects observed in earlier experiments into one unifying theory expressed mathematically in four equations. Electricity and magnetism could no longer be viewed as two separate phenomena but as features of a more general electromagnetism. Measuring the speed of light (Foucault) and verifying the waves (Hertz) were other people's work.

questions.q: Which of Maxwell's four equations introduces the permeability of free space and states that a magnetic field is produced by an electric current or by a changing electric flux?
options: Gauss's law, which describes the electric flux produced by charges
Gauss's law for magnetic fields, which states there are no magnetic monopoles
Faraday's law, which describes the electric field induced by a changing magnetic field
The Ampere-Maxwell law, which introduces the permeability of free space
questions.explanation: The Ampere-Maxwell law is a little like Faraday's law but deals with changing electric flux: a magnetic field is produced by an electric current or by a changing electric flux. This law introduces the permeability of free space. Faraday's law is the partner that describes the electric field induced by a changing magnetic field.

questions.q: From memory, explain what is meant by the permittivity of free space.
keyPoints: The permittivity of free space is a constant in Gauss's law for electricity.
It is the constant of proportionality between the electric flux passing through an enclosed space and the charge enclosed by the space.
It is the electric partner of the permeability of free space, which plays the same role for magnetic fields.
questions.explanation: The textbook's model answer: the permittivity of free space is the constant of proportionality between the electric flux passing through an enclosed space and the charge enclosed by the space. If you tied it to electric flux and enclosed charge, grade yourself Good or Easy.

questions.q: Calculate the speed of electromagnetic waves given that the permittivity of free space is 8.854 × 10^-12 and the permeability of free space is 4π × 10^-7.
questions.given: permittivity of free space \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.854 \times 10^{-12}\),  permeability of free space \(\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\)
questions.explanation: Apply \(v = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}\): multiply the two constants, square root, then reciprocal. This is the textbook's own sample-problem value, 2.998 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, normally rounded to 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Don't forget it is the reciprocal of the square root, not the square root itself.

questions.q: Maxwell's wave equation gave the speed of electromagnetic waves as 2.998 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Why was this figure so significant?
options: It was far larger than any speed previously measured, so it was assumed to be an error
It is equal to the speed of light, a fact noticed by Maxwell that led to his proposal that light is an electromagnetic wave
It depended only on the permeability of free space, proving magnetism alone causes light
It matched the speed of sound, showing light and sound are the same phenomenon
questions.explanation: The textbook states this figure is equal to the speed of light, a fact noticed by Maxwell that led to his proposal that light was an electromagnetic wave. The two constants come from electric and magnetic experiments independent of light, so the matching speed is powerful, independent evidence.

questions.q: According to Maxwell's theory, what is required to produce an electromagnetic wave that propagates through space?
options: A constant DC current flowing through a straight wire
A stationary electric charge sitting on an insulator
An oscillating (vibrating) electric charge, such as an accelerating charge
A steady magnetic field from a permanent magnet
questions.explanation: To produce an electromagnetic wave that propagates through space, an oscillating (vibrating) electric charge is required. The moving charge forms an oscillating current that induces an oscillating magnetic field, which induces an electric field; these self-perpetuating fields radiate out at 2.998 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. A constant DC current produces no wave.

questions.q: In 1983 the speed of light was declared to be exactly 299 792 458 m s⁻¹. Explain how the metre and the second are defined as a result. (3 marks)
questions.modelAnswer: Because the speed of light is constant, it was set as an exact standard of 299 792 458 m s⁻¹. With this value fixed, one metre is defined as how far light travels in a vacuum in 1/299 792 458 of a second. The second is defined independently from a precise natural standard: caesium-133 atoms have an energy transition that occurs 9 192 631 770 times per second, and one second is the time taken for that many transitions, which is the basis of atomic clocks.

criteria.descriptor: States the speed of light is fixed/declared exactly as 299 792 458 m s⁻¹.
Defines the metre as the distance light travels in 1/299 792 458 of a second.
Defines the second using the 9 192 631 770 transitions of caesium-133 (atomic clock standard).

questions.explanation: Because the speed of light is now declared exactly, it is no longer measured; instead the metre is defined from it, and the second from the caesium-133 transition that occurs 9 192 631 770 times per second.

questions.q: Which statement correctly identifies who did what in the story of the speed of light?
options: Maxwell measured the speed of light experimentally; Hertz predicted electromagnetic waves on paper
Maxwell predicted the speed from theory; Hertz verified electromagnetic waves by experiment after Maxwell had died
Both Maxwell and Hertz measured the speed using rotating mirrors
Hertz predicted the waves from theory; Maxwell later detected them with a loop antenna
questions.explanation: Maxwell predicted the speed of light from pure theory and concluded light is an electromagnetic wave; he never made or detected one. Hertz, working in the 1880s after Maxwell's death, produced and detected the waves and measured their speed. The mnemonic: Maxwell predicts, Hertz proves.

questions.q: From memory: why is Hertz's receiver loop sparking, with no power source of its own, the proof that an electromagnetic wave crossed the room?
keyPoints: The receiver was just a loop of wire with a small gap, connected to no battery or power source.
To make a spark jump the gap, a current must be induced; by Faraday's law that needs a changing magnetic field threading the loop.
With nothing connecting transmitter and receiver, the changing field must have arrived as a radiated electromagnetic wave carrying energy across empty space.
questions.explanation: The headline fact is 'no power source of its own'. The spark in an unpowered loop can only come from an induced current, which requires a changing magnetic field that travelled across the room as a wave. Leave out 'no power source' and you miss the entire point.

questions.q: A microwave transmitter of frequency 10.5 GHz is aimed at a metal reflector, forming a standing wave. Adjacent nodes are found 14.3 mm apart. Calculate the speed of the electromagnetic waves.
working: Adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart, so \(\lambda = 2 \times \text{node spacing}\)
questions.explanation: The one piece you cannot get wrong: adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart, so double the node spacing to get the wavelength, then use v = fλ. Forgetting the factor of two halves your answer to 1.5 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
